messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Multivariate Multiple Regression (multi_normal + wishart)
parts:
I'm combining a users list and dev list post here (see
below).


Matt (user):

Thanks for the careful error report -- it helps us
immensely.

I believe that one of the size tests is failing
(mu must be same size as y, and the rows and columns
of Omega must be the same).

This is puzzling given your model, the declarations
for which are

> matrix[nData, nVars] y;
> matrix[nData, nVars] mu;
> cov_matrix[nVars] Omega;

seem to me to be compatible with the usage:

> col(y, i) ~ multi_normal(col(mu,i), Omega);



Daniel (dev):

We need to get more information into the
test messages that come back. I assume one of
the check_size_match functions is balking here, but
I can't tell which one from the message. Could
we replace "function" with something more error-specific?


Ben (dev):

Could this be in the way we call multi_normal_cholesky
from multi_normal_log? If multi_normal_log doesn't
throw a sizing error, neither should multi_normal_cholesky.
(That is, we want to test size issues as early as possible
for the purpose of user error reporting.)

- Bob


On 1/30/13 6:54 AM, Matt wrote:
> Hi!
> I've been trying to get a multivariate regression to work in STAN, similar to the model depicted here in JAGS
> (http://jackman.stanford.edu/classes/BASS/92plain.bug) but with more dependent variables and using Wishart priors. This
> is the error message I get:
>
> Error in sampler$call_sampler(args_list[[i]]) :
>
> Error in function stan::prob::multi_normal_cholesky_log(l): i and j must be same. Found i=235, j=3
>
> error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done
>
>
> Below is the code. It runs ok if I replace the multi_normal in the likelihood with a regular normal or t distribution -
> then I adjust it to loop over the dependent variables and data points, and replace the Omega by a series of independent
> standard deviations obtained for each variable. I'm not sure what to try next. Any help to get this going would be much
> appreciated. I've attached a small chunk of the data if it helps.
>
> Matt
>
>
> |
>
> MRegMod = '
> data {
> int<lower=1> nData;
> int<lower=1> nVars;
> real x3[nData];
> matrix[nData, nVars] y;
> matrix[nVars, nVars] Imat;
> vector[nVars] b0p;
> vector[nVars] b3p;
> }
> parameters {
> vector[nVars] b0;
> vector[nVars] b3;
> cov_matrix[nVars] Omega;
> cov_matrix[nVars] Omega0;
> cov_matrix[nVars] Omega3;
> real<lower=0,upper=100> sd[nVars];
> }
> transformed parameters {
> matrix[nData, nVars] mu;
> for ( np in 1:nVars){
> for ( i in 1:nData){
> mu[i, np] <- b0[np] + b3[np] * x3[i];
> }
> }
> }
>
> model {
> //Priors
> b0 ~ multi_normal(b0p , Omega0);
> b3 ~ multi_normal(b3p , Omega3);
> Omega0 ~ inv_wishart(nVars+1, Imat);
> Omega3 ~ inv_wishart(nVars+1, Imat);
>
> //Likelihood
> for(i in 1:nData){
> col(y, i) ~ multi_normal(col(mu,i), Omega);
> }
> Omega ~ inv_wishart(nVars+1, Imat);
> }
> '
> |

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: [stan-users] Multivariate Multiple Regression (multi_normal + wishart)
parts:
On Wed, Jan 30, 2013 at 11:31 AM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
I'm combining a users list and dev list post here (see
below).


Matt (user):

Thanks for the careful error report -- it helps us
immensely.

I believe that one of the size tests is failing
(mu must be same size as y, and the rows and columns
of Omega must be the same).

This is puzzling given your model, the declarations
for which are

>      matrix[nData, nVars] y;
>      matrix[nData, nVars] mu;
>      cov_matrix[nVars] Omega;

seem to me to be compatible with the usage:


>        col(y, i) ~ multi_normal(col(mu,i), Omega);

I believe this should be: 

row(y, i) ~ multi_normal(row(mu,i), Omega);

In the above, col(y,i) and col(mu,i) are vector[nData] but Omega is cov_matrix[nVars].

Cheers,
Marcus
